newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-U.S. TO HOST DAVIS CUP SEMIFINAL ON HARDCOURT.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-U.S. TO HOST DAVIS CUP SEMIFINAL ON HARDCOURT.

text.p: The United States will host the Davis Cup semifinal against Australia in September on hardcourt, increasing the likelihood that Pete Sampras will lead their challenge, Tennis Australia (TA) said on Wednesday.
The tie will be played in either Raleigh, North Carolina, or Washington DC from September 19-21, TA said in a statement.
Australia non-playing captain John Newcombe said the United States decision, as hosts, to play on one of Sampras' favourite surfaces suggested the world number one would take part.
"We want the U.S. to field their best team, so for the (ruling body) USTA to select hardcourt indicates that Pete Sampras will play," Newcombe said in the statement.
The United States had been expected to opt for the slower clay surface if Sampras did not make himself available, TA said.
Australia reached the semifinals with a 5-0 rout of Czech Republic earlier this month, while the Americans overcame Netherlands 4-1.
The winner will meet either Sweden or Italy in the Davis Cup final in late November.
